messages.content: The Tuesday evening flight is still the front-runner, so compare hotels for June 16 through June 19. The workshop is near Union Station and starts at 8:00 each morning. I can expense up to $225 a night before tax.

I found three workable refundable rates for three nights. The Oxford Hotel is $223 per night, $669 before tax and $773.36 total; it is about a five-minute walk from the workshop. Hyatt Place Denver/Downtown is $196 per night, $588 before tax and $679.73 total; allow roughly 12-18 minutes by light rail and walking, or 8-12 minutes by rideshare. Hampton Inn & Suites Denver-Speer Boulevard is $174 per night, $522 before tax and $603.43 total; it is about 12-18 minutes by rideshare in normal morning traffic. All three fit the nightly cap.
What are the cancellation deadlines? The flight is only being held, and I don't want a hotel charge if that changes tomorrow.

The Oxford rate can be canceled without penalty until 6:00 p.m. Mountain Time on June 12; after that, the penalty is one night's room and tax. Hyatt Place allows free cancellation until 11:59 p.m. Mountain Time on June 15, with a one-night room-and-tax penalty afterward. Hampton allows free cancellation until 6:00 p.m. Mountain Time on June 14, also followed by a one-night room-and-tax penalty. None of these rates shows prepayment, but the hotel may place a temporary authorization at check-in.
So the closest one costs about $94 more than Hyatt in total and gives me three fewer days to cancel?

Correct. The Oxford total is $93.63 higher, and its free-cancellation window closes on June 12 rather than late June 15. Its practical advantage is the short walk: you could leave around 7:45 and still have comfortable margin. From Hyatt Place, I would plan to leave around 7:25 by light rail or 7:30 by rideshare.
How reliable is that light-rail trip? I don't want an inexpensive room to create a problem at 7:30 in the morning.

The route is short, but the end-to-end estimate depends on the walk to the station and waiting for the next train. Scheduled service should get you there comfortably if you leave by 7:25, though a disruption could erase the margin. A rideshare is the simpler backup; budgeting $12-$18 each morning would add about $24-$36 for Wednesday and Thursday, while Friday's checkout trip can be combined with your luggage plans.
Even with two rideshares, Hyatt is still cheaper than the Oxford. Is Hampton worth considering, or is that too much extra travel for three early starts?

Hampton saves another $76.30 versus Hyatt, but it has no especially useful rail route to the venue, so you would likely use rideshare each morning. Three trips at roughly $14-$22 apiece would absorb $42-$66 of the savings, and traffic introduces more variability. It remains the lowest-cost option, but Hyatt offers a better balance of total cost, transportation choices, and cancellation flexibility.
Rank Hyatt first, then the Oxford as the backup if the workshop address turns out to be a few blocks farther from Union Station. Drop Hampton.

That ranking makes sense. Hyatt Place is first at $196 nightly, $588 before tax and $679.73 total, with free cancellation through June 15 at 11:59 p.m. Mountain Time. The Oxford is second at $223 nightly, $669 before tax and $773.36 total, with free cancellation through June 12 at 6:00 p.m. Mountain Time. Hampton is removed from the shortlist.
Before I move forward, check the dates against the flight plan and tell me what still needs confirmation.

The hotel dates align with the leading itinerary: check in Tuesday, June 16 after the 8:21 p.m. arrival, stay three nights, and check out Friday, June 19 before the workshop and 6:25 p.m. return flight. Before reserving Hyatt, confirm the final workshop street address, the live $196 refundable rate, the $679.73 all-in total, and that cancellation remains available through late June 15 without prepayment. Also recheck the held flight's $438 fare, Wi-Fi notation, and restrictions before purchase. If the venue moves enough to make the morning trip impractical, compare the Oxford again before its earlier cancellation deadline. Nothing has been booked or charged.
